hard_spots.kind: classical Chinese tags and learned allusion
hard_spots.why_hard: Two quoted tags do documentary work: whenever he drank alone he finished a whole jar, and three hundred mu by the wall half planted with millet. The first measures excess; the second measures wealth. Both sound like quoted Chinese. English must keep them visibly quoted and quantitative, not smooth them into description.

Bamboo wife (chikufujin) to lean on in heat, white-feather fan, long hemp robe with loose sash, jar-measure (u / ichiou), unglazed jar, thin cord (hosobiki). The tale enjoys specifying them. Generic old-China paraphrase would impoverish that scholar’s texture.

Western Regions, west of the Congling, Hodoji temple, yellow robe, bronze earring, turkey-like squat. Period wording (banzo, barbarian monk) marks outsider status functionally. English must neither exoticize into menace nor mute into neutral monk; editor fork on strength of period marking.

Black cataract and byouen (likely genital ailment) cited as instant miraculous cures. Exact modern equivalents are uncertain and unnecessary; English needs plain period-flavoured terms with a note, not a confident clinical diagnosis.

Cao Mengde curing soldiers’ thirst by saying there is a plum grove ahead. Liu knows the bookish trick and finds it useless against real thirst. The joke needs minimal annotation; over-explaining kills the disproportion.

The lump climbs like an earthworm, shifts like a gecko, slips out like a loach; the expelled worm is like a small salamander the colour of red mud, swimming and seeming to drink. Deliberately flat and faintly disgusting. English must not ennoble into grotesque poetry or cool into clinical terms.
Pochiyari, the small splash as something drops into wine in the jar. Tiny sound is the proof of expulsion. Needs a small, unshowy English splash, not a comic plop.
Three hundred mu of fields, three-sun worm, one jar at a sitting. The marvel is measured. Keep measures with minimal help in notes; converting to acres/inches makes it vaguer and more fable-like.
Didacticism appears in English in the Japanese and is part of the closing joke and refusal. It must stay visibly imported and slightly pedantic, not naturalised to moralising.
Gonen shigatsu, April of the fifth year (Taisho 5, 1916). Looks like a classical tale’s colophon and publication marker at once. English must not resolve it into a fuller date than the text gives.

motifs.english: Keep one fixed English term wine worm everywhere, never varied. The ending argues over that single word (disease, fortune, self), so varying it unbuilds the argument.
motifs.why: The creature is at once diagnosis, cure-object and moral counter. The text insists on the same two characters throughout.

motifs.english: Let heat accumulate in the same register: heat, blazing sun, noon, drought, steaming, leaden reflection, burning skin. Do not vary away for elegance; the reader should feel half-roasted before thirst starts.
motifs.motif: heat at noon that will not move
motifs.why: Frame and suffering are both written as weather. Opening tableau, noon stillness and Liu’s burning skin form one continuous scorch.

motifs.english: Keep the same flat stillness wording: shut mouths, no movement, held breath, clay images. Return it emptied in the decline report.
motifs.why: Three men holding silence like temple images sets the tale’s pressure; the same vocabulary of stillness returns as Liu’s emptied life.

motifs.english: Keep jar, wine and smell as a measured set: a jar at a sitting, a jar at the pillow, wine the worm swims in and drinks, smell that thickens by the minute. Do not substitute cup, bottle or alcohol.
motifs.why: Wine is everywhere quantified. The cure uses the same measure as the excess, and the proof swims in it.

motifs.english: Keep the low animals as given, in order, without upgrading: earthworm, gecko, loach for the ascent and exit; small salamander the colour of red mud for the thing in the wine. Their flat oddity is the evidence.
motifs.why: Deliberately unliterary zoology against the bookish frame. The horror and comedy are in the exact lowness.

motifs.english: Keep the three answers formally parallel and equally weighted, increasingly metaphysical, with the third dissolving the first two. Do not make them a crescendo with the third as truth.
motifs.why: Borrowed didactic machinery assembled and left running empty. Parallel form is the point; livelier variation would hide it.

narration.english_tense: Simple past as default for narrated events; keep general truths and the three morals in present. Do not use a historic present for the opening tableau — get its held stillness from short stative past sentences held a beat too long, then narrow to close past-progressive sensation in section three.
narration.frame: Image first, provenance second, explanation third. Held noon tableau with explanation withheld (p2-p7), aside that of course this is not Japan but Changshan China (p8), flashback to chess game interrupted by maid announcing visitor (p11-p42), return to yard for suffering and expulsion (p44-p51), three-year-later report and listed morals with refusal to choose (p53-p59).
narration.narrator: Extradiegetic bookish reteller performing a Chinese strange tale; not a participant. Stages erudite tableau, supplies rumour and back-story, intrudes coolly with an essayist comparison (schooling in p42) and closing Didacticism disclaimer (p59).
narration.person: Third person throughout, with explicit first-person (jibun) only in the closing disavowal in p59
narration.tense_habits: Opening tableau in descriptive present-like literary forms (de aru, te iru); back-story dialogue and treatment preparation in past (ta); bodily suffering in immediate progressive and iterative present-like sensation with past reflection; decline report in resultative past to present state
timeline: Earlier the same summer day: Liu and Mr Sun play go leaning on the bamboo wife; the maid announces the Hodoji monk (p11-p18)
Noon the same day on the Liu threshing-yard: Liu lies naked and bound, monk watches, Mr Sun watches; the worm climbs and drops into the jar (p2-p7, p40-p51)
Three years after the expulsion to the time of telling: Liu cannot bear wine-smell, health and three hundred mu drain away, he ploughs inexpertly day by day (p53-p54)
Time of telling: narrator collects the three current Changshan explanations and declines to choose; dated fifth year fourth month (p55-p60)

part_summaries.summary: Part One. Unbearable summer over roofs, swallows’ nests and drooping hemp and millet. On a threshing-yard at noon three silent motionless men: a fat naked man bound with cord with an unglazed jar at his pillow, a dark-skinned foreign monk in yellow robe shooing flies with a red-handled whisk, a thin-bearded scholar in long robe fanning himself apart under the eaves. Held stillness like clay temple images. Aside: of course this is not Japan but the Liu threshing-yard at Changshan, China.

Part Two. Flashback explanation. The naked man is Liu Dacheng, rich landowner of three hundred mu who drinks a jar at a sitting and never gets drunk. Playing go with fellow drinker Mr Sun, he receives the Hodoji barbarian monk famous for miraculous cures. The monk asks if he likes wine, says he never gets drunk because a wine worm is in his belly, and offers a drugless, needless, charm-less cure: lie naked motionless in the sun. Liu consents, is bound, a jar of wine is set at his pillow, Mr Sun stays to watch.

Part Three. The cure as suffered body. Sweat stings the eyes for the first time, skin prickles without elasticity, thirst grows while wine-smell from the pillow jar thickens by the minute and bookish remedies fail. A soft lump creeps up the gullet like earthworm and gecko and slips out like a loach with a small splash into the jar. The monk unties him saying the worm is out. All three peer in: a three-sun red-mud-coloured salamander-like thing with mouth and eyes swims in the wine seemingly drinking. Liu feels sick.

Part Four. Report three years on. The cure worked at once: Liu cannot drink or bear the smell. Health, colour, hair and estate have drained together; fields mostly in other hands; he ploughs inexpertly. Narrator lists three representative Changshan answers — worm was fortune lost through folly, worm was disease so poverty-with-life is happiness, worm was neither because Liu-minus-wine is nothing so expulsion was self-killing — and says he does not know which is right, imitating Chinese novelists’ Didacticism. Dated fifth year fourth month.

data.say: A perfect noon cure that is also a slow killing, told in two weathers and refused a moral: keep cure and ruin in one level tone and let the three borrowed answers cancel each other.

style_sheet.annotation_density: Sparse. Note only what the sentence cannot give: mu and sun as measures, jar-measure, bamboo wife, Congling/Western Regions, Hodoji, byouen uncertainty, plum-grove allusion, Didacticism as imported English. Never note what context supplies or to explain the moral.
style_sheet.author_voice: Young Taisho sinophile performing erudition: kanji-dense, name- and measure-heavy, fond of quoted tags and furigana glosses, dry and faintly disgusting. Learned, not exotic; bookish frame against deliberately low body writing. Guard everywhere against ennoblement into elegance, chinoiserie or wisdom.
style_sheet.honorifics_and_names: Keep the relationship in address: Liu Dacheng on first mention then Liu; the monk as the barbarian monk, never a personal name; Sun Sensei throughout, never Mr Sun alone, because Sensei carries the Confucian status comedy. Keep name order family-first. For Chinese places and names use pinyin in text with Japanese reading in note where the gloss matters (Changshan [text glosses Chozan], Liu Dacheng, Sun Xiansheng), to keep the pseudo-record flavour without inventing readings.
style_sheet.keep_in_japanese: Keep in Japanese with note help only where English has no equivalent doing the same work: mu, sun, hosobiki (thin cord), unglazed jar (suyaki no kame), bamboo wife, white-feather fan. Keep temple and reign-flavoured titles as transliterated proper nouns (Hodoji, Western Regions, Congling). Keep Didacticism in English exactly as the source has it.
style_sheet.quotation: Japanese kagikakko for speech and quoted tags become English double quotes; quoted Chinese tags stay quoted and slightly stiff to mark borrowing. No mock-antique thees or ver Cometlys.
style_sheet.register: Learned and slightly bookish for frame and back-story, specifying not smoothing; flat and unliterary for skin, sweat, thirst and nausea. Dry aside voice for the two narrator intrusions (schooling comparison, Didacticism disclaimer). Nobody warmed up; nobody given interiority except sweat, thirst and nausea.
style_sheet.ruby_and_italics: Furigana glosses (swallow, threshing-yard, wine worm, temple and place readings) are reading aids, not double terms; do not carry both into English. Use italics sparingly for quoted Chinese tags and for Didacticism to show it as imported; otherwise roman transliterations in roman type.
